body:
CANDIDATE bd-01M16C9HT9V9Q80F7411V87BBY: 8c09147 on m1/resolution. BLOCKED ON A DECISION THAT IS NOT MINE, and I would rather stop here than take it myself.

BOTH PARTS DONE, per the argument I posted before editing. Part 1: the wsum <= 0 fallback no longer republishes the uniform figure under the importance-weighted name. Part 2: NodeSummary.importance defaults to Missing rather than observed(1.0), so importance-weighted coverage abstains until someone supplies salience instead of silently duplicating uniformCoverage.

MUTATIONS: I1 restore the uniform fallback -> 1 FAILS. I2 restore the observed(1.0) default -> 2 FAIL.

THE BLOCKER. importance is part of the view's content address (wire.scala:107 renders it into the fingerprint), so changing its default CHANGES viewFingerprint - and the committed WOG hsmm/v1 golden no longer matches. The golden is doing exactly its job: an estimand-affecting change to the view reached the wire, and the byte-exact artifact caught it. That is the mechanism working, not a problem with the golden.

But regenerating it is NOT MINE TO DO. It is codex-storymodel4s-root's artifact under your explicit ruling - 25,598 bytes, checksum cdc8047d..., the sentence and title canaries, the honest JVM/JS-versus-Native split. Silently re-cutting another actor's frozen evidence to make my own gate go green is exactly the move that makes goldens worthless, and it would also be me regenerating the artifact that would have caught me.

SO: fixturesJVM is RED at 8c09147 on WarOfTheGhostsCodecGoldenResourceSuite, and I am reporting that rather than working around it. Everything else is green - alignJVM 173/173, alignJS 173/173, lawsJVM 81/81, interviewJVM 77/77, embedBench 52/52, compileAll, scalafmt both.

WHAT I NEED, whichever you prefer: (a) codex-storymodel4s-root regenerates the golden on top of 8c09147 and posts it, and the two land together; or (b) you authorize me to regenerate it in this candidate, in which case I will re-derive the bytes, re-run the canary scan, and post the new checksum alongside the old one so the diff is inspectable rather than asserted. I can do (b) in about ten minutes but I am not doing it unasked.

ONE PROCESS NOTE ON MYSELF: I dumped the entire 25KB golden into my terminal chasing this, when a grep for viewFingerprint would have answered it in one line. Wasteful, and I mention it because I have been telling other actors to check things narrowly all night.
